section_headings: What are the genetics of Roswell 47?

article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Jealousy × C-Note
Breeder: Decibel Gardens
THC Content: 28%
CBD Content: Typically low
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Berry, sweet cream, pepper, citrus, earth
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: mid October
Indoor Yield: Medium
Outdoor Yield: Medium
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Few contemporary cannabis strains have built a reputation as quickly through actual competition results as Roswell 47 . Created by California cultivator and breeder Decibel Gardens, this dark-colored hybrid combines Jealousy with the company’s proprietary C-Note genetics, producing flower centered on rich fruit, pepper, earth and a distinctly modern Gelato-influenced character. The strain has become one of Decibel Gardens’ signature proprietary varieties, a status reflected by the company’s continued use of Roswell 47 in its breeding program. Decibel Gardens itself emphasizes in-house genetics and careful cultivation, drying, trimming and storage as central parts of its approach to finished cannabis.

The cultivar’s reputation is not based simply on marketing. Roswell 47 earned the California MJBowl Trophy for Best in Category in flower and also took first place as the Indoor Flower MVP at the 2025 MJBowl, an expert-judged competition presented by MJBiz and Budist. That achievement helps explain why this weed has attracted attention among consumers who prioritize terpene intensity, flower structure and overall smoking quality rather than THC percentage alone. Roswell 47 belongs to the modern dessert-and-gas school of marijuana breeding, but its darker berry and pepper characteristics give it considerably more personality than a straightforward sweet Gelato cross.
Genetics and Lineage

Roswell 47 comes from Jealousy × C-Note, with Decibel Gardens responsible for the breeding. Independent coverage of the cultivar identifies that same parentage, while Decibel Gardens has publicly discussed Roswell 47 as one of the proprietary genetic lines that helped establish its portfolio. The combination is significant because both parents carry substantial Gelato influence, yet they approach that genetic family from different directions.

Jealousy descends from Gelato 41 crossed with Sherbet Bx1, giving it the dense flower structure, dessert sweetness, peppery character and colorful pigmentation commonly associated with premium California cannabis genetics. C-Note, meanwhile, is another Decibel Gardens project associated with Gelato family and blueberry-influenced ancestry. Bringing the two together concentrates the creamy, resinous characteristics of modern Gelato breeding while introducing darker fruit, berry and earth tones that distinguish the finished cultivar from the many sweet strains occupying the same genetic neighborhood.

Rather than becoming simply another candy-heavy hybrid, Roswell 47 developed a much stranger sensory identity. The flower frequently expresses deep purple coloration and a heavily resin-coated appearance, traits that complement the extraterrestrial branding surrounding the strain. More importantly, the genetic pairing produces a flavor that moves from ripe fruit and sweetness into black pepper, earth and gas. This combination of attractive morphology and complex aroma appears to have been deliberate; Decibel Gardens has continued working Roswell 47 back into newer crosses, demonstrating that it functions as breeding material as well as finished commercial flower.
Effects and Experience

Roswell 47 tends to begin on the brighter side of the hybrid spectrum. The early portion of the experience can bring a noticeable cerebral lift, greater interest in conversation and a pleasant sense of mental momentum. Rather than immediately pushing the consumer toward the couch, the onset can feel socially engaging and euphoric. That quality makes the strain potentially well suited to music, movies, gaming, creative hobbies or relaxed gatherings where a strong marijuana experience is wanted without instant sedation.

The physical character becomes more noticeable as the session progresses. A spreading heaviness can emerge through the body while the mental effects remain comparatively clear, producing an unusual combination of relaxation and awareness. This transition is one of the cultivar’s more appealing traits: the high does not necessarily stay energetic, yet it also does not behave like a purely sleepy indica. Depending on dose and individual tolerance, the later stages may become noticeably heavier, accompanied by increased appetite and a desire to settle into a comfortable setting.

Potency deserves respect. Roswell 47 is generally encountered as premium high-THC flower, and excessive consumption may turn an otherwise balanced experience into dizziness, mental fog, dry mouth or anxiety. Newer consumers should start conservatively, particularly when smoking fresh indoor flower or concentrated versions made from the cultivar. Cannabis effects can differ substantially between individuals, and a person’s tolerance often matters more than the strain’s marketing category.
Medical Benefits

There are no clinical trials establishing Roswell 47 as a treatment for any specific disease, and its competition success should not be confused with medical evidence. Even so, some medical marijuana consumers may find its combination of euphoria and physical relaxation useful when their goal is temporary relief from everyday stress or difficulty settling down. The later body-heavy portion of the experience may also be attractive to people who prefer cannabis that relaxes without immediately producing complete mental shutdown.

THC-rich marijuana can affect pain perception, appetite, mood and sleep, but those broader properties do not prove that this particular cultivar will produce a predictable therapeutic outcome. Roswell 47’s strong sensory qualities may make it enjoyable for patients who have trouble with appetite, while its transition from mental uplift toward physical calm could fit evening use for some consumers. Responses remain highly individual, especially with high-potency flower.

Anyone using cannabis alongside prescription medication or for a diagnosed medical condition should approach the strain cautiously. High doses of THC can increase heart rate, impair coordination and occasionally worsen anxiety or dizziness. The safest way to evaluate Roswell 47 medically is by paying attention to the cannabinoid information on the specific package and using small quantities until the individual’s response is understood.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The aroma is where Roswell 47 becomes especially distinctive. Opening well-cured flower can reveal a dark fruit character reminiscent of ripe berries rather than the bright tropical sweetness found in many newer hybrids. Sweet cream and subtle citrus sit underneath, while cracked pepper, damp earth and gas provide a darker foundation. The result smells rich rather than sugary, with enough savory depth to keep the fruit from becoming candy-like.

Breaking apart the buds generally exposes more of the pungent side of the profile. Pepper and earthy cannabis aromas become stronger, followed by creamy Gelato-like sweetness and occasional citrus sharpness. That layered aromatic structure helps explain why the strain has performed so well in judged competitions: it develops across several sensory directions rather than presenting one dominant note.

On the palate, berry sweetness often arrives early before giving way to pepper, cream and earthy gas. The finish can linger with a slightly spicy, almost savory quality. Consumers accustomed to dessert strains may recognize the Gelato-family influence, but Roswell 47 is considerably darker and less confectionery than many relatives. Its flavor feels closer to berry cream layered over peppery fuel than straightforward fruit candy.
Growing Information

Public cultivation information for the authentic Decibel Gardens Roswell 47 remains limited. The breeder maintains the cultivar as part of its proprietary genetics portfolio, and no authoritative public grow sheet establishes a universal flowering period, indoor yield, outdoor harvest date or plant height. For that reason, precise claims such as a guaranteed eight-week finish or a particular grams-per-square-meter yield should be treated cautiously unless they come directly from a verified Decibel Gardens release.

What can be inferred from the finished commercial flower is that the plant is capable of producing dense, highly resinous buds with dramatic pigmentation under controlled indoor conditions. Growers working with legitimate genetics should pay close attention to canopy airflow because tightly structured flowers can retain moisture if humidity remains excessive late in bloom. Strategic pruning and good spacing can help expose productive flowering sites while reducing stagnant air inside the canopy.

Post-harvest handling is especially important with a cultivar prized for its aroma. Decibel Gardens specifically emphasizes drying, storage, trimming and packaging as essential parts of presenting its genetics at their full potential. Drying Roswell 47 too rapidly could flatten the berry-and-pepper character that gives the plant its identity, while excessive heat may strip away volatile aromatic compounds. A controlled dry followed by a careful cure is therefore just as important as producing visually impressive flowers during cultivation.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Roswell 47?
Roswell 47 is Jealousy crossed with C-Note. Decibel Gardens bred the cultivar as part of its proprietary genetics program.
Who bred Roswell 47?
Decibel Gardens created Roswell 47. The California cultivator has continued to feature the strain prominently within its proprietary genetic lineup and subsequent breeding work.
Is Roswell 47 indica or sativa?

It is best described as a hybrid. The experience can begin with euphoric and mentally engaging effects before gradually developing stronger physical relaxation, making a simple indica-or-sativa label less informative than describing the progression of the high.
What does Roswell 47 taste like?

The strain combines dark berry sweetness with cream, pepper, citrus, earth and gas. Its Gelato-related ancestry contributes a smooth dessert quality, but the peppery and earthy finish prevents it from tasting like a conventional candy strain.
Has Roswell 47 won cannabis awards?
Yes. Roswell 47 by Decibel Gardens won the California MJBowl Trophy for Best in Category in flower and took first place as the Indoor Flower MVP at the 2025 MJBowl.
Final Thoughts on Roswell 47

Roswell 47 demonstrates what can happen when familiar modern cannabis genetics are selected toward a genuinely recognizable outcome. Jealousy and C-Note both bring Gelato-family traits into the cross, yet the finished cultivar moves beyond basic creamy sweetness. Dark berry, pepper, earth and gas provide contrast, while the unusually deep coloration and resin production give the flower visual character to match its aroma.

Its competitive record strengthens the case that this hybrid deserves attention beyond novelty branding. Winning top honors in a judged flower category suggests that the cultivar succeeds across aroma, flavor, appearance and overall experience rather than relying on a single laboratory potency number. For cannabis enthusiasts interested in modern California genetics, Roswell 47 offers a useful example of how thoughtful selection can transform familiar Gelato ancestry into something much more individual: potent weed with dark fruit, peppery depth, impressive flower quality and an identity strong enough to stand on its own.
